releaseNotes: PR-4b of the 2026-08 graph-consolidation audit's thin-domain rebalancing: domain.words owns the repo's writing-quality standard (cited by 14+ files across 8 other domains) but its mechanical enforcement primitives (tooling/lib/no-slop-rules.ts — banned words, 13 slop-pattern regexes, an em-dash budget, all parsed live from knowledge/words/no-slop-writing.md so the two can't drift) were never wired into a gate, leaving the reference's own §2 promise — that the rules also cover 'this repo's own public docs' — unenforced. Added validation/business/words/check-no-slop.ts (check:no-slop), scanning README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, .github/SECURITY.md, and .github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at error and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md at warning, exactly matching the reference's documented tier split. Verified by injecting a banned word into README.md and watching the gate fail, then reverting. Fixed a citation bug the same read surfaced: the reference's own §2 line named this surface 'trust/SECURITY.md', a directory-move artifact from an unrelated reorganization — the real file lives at .github/SECURITY.md.

This exact validator existed before (2026-07-25) and was deliberately deleted during the autonomous-business-runtime rebuild (U1-U11, PR #114): docs/plans/attachments/2026-08-port-ledger.md dispositioned it 'drop' as 'the purest word-pattern validator ... graded prose form, never a verifiable fact.' Ran that reversal through llm-council before rebuilding rather than silently resurrecting it: the council's unanimous finding was that the 'drop' philosophy was never applied consistently — two sibling validators in the same directory (check-app-copy.ts, check-founder-copy.ts) were dispositioned 'port' (strip the word-pattern half) and remain fully unchanged, still running the identical kind of logic, two months later. The ledger row now records this reversal and its reasoning explicitly rather than a silent overwrite; a tracked follow-up (not a someday) is filed to either execute the siblings' original port plan or formally revise their disposition too.

Extracted tooling/lib/git-root.ts (findGitRoot, shared with check-version-discipline.ts, which previously carried its own private copy) since check-no-slop.ts needed the same real-repo-root lookup and duplicating it would only diverge later, per this repo's own recurring lesson about copy-pasted helpers.

Wired check:no-slop into both package.json manifests, tooling/lib/audit-plan.ts, and run-launchbench.ts's knownValidators; added 7 fixture cases (validation/repository/fixtures/repo-gates.fixtures.ts) covering the pass path, the missing-file case, the error-tier failure, the warning-tier demotion, a non-banned-word mechanical slop pattern, and the always-advisory empty-adverb rule.
